areas.name: Reading
areas.definition: The HTTP reading-list product serving readers.

root.responsibility: Owns request tracing, demo access admission, route handling, published-book filtering and SQLite persistence.
root.runs: Operators start python server.py as a long-lived HTTP server; readers call GET /books.
root.why: Without it readers cannot retrieve the published reading list.

projects.name: Reading API
projects.summary: One HTTP reading-list product with internal domain and persistence modules.
projects.purpose: Readers retrieve published books; the domain and SQLite adapter run only inside this service and are not independent products.

system.name: Reading API
system.summary: A single HTTP service returns published books from a SQLite reading list.
system.purpose: Readers request published book titles through an ordered trace and authentication pipeline; a local Compose declaration adds an HTTP reverse proxy.

externals.name: SQLite
externals.role: Embedded book database persisted by the API.

flows.label: HTTP GET /books
flows.detail: Reader submits the public demo access header.

flows.label: SQLite file I/O
flows.detail: The embedded sqlite3 driver reads book rows.

views.title: Reading-list request
views.question: Where can GET /books stop before storage?
views.scope: One GET /books request, with and without X-Demo-Access: reader.
views.summary: server.py registers MIDDLEWARE = (trace, authenticate); dispatch starts at route and wraps reversed(MIDDLEWARE), so trace calls authenticate then route. Responses unwind through the wrappers before do_GET serializes JSON. The graph separates entry and return phases of those calls.

nodes.label: GET /books
nodes.detail: BaseHTTPRequestHandler.do_GET builds the request and invokes dispatch.

nodes.label: Trace request
nodes.detail: trace calls next_handler(request) before adding X-Request-Id; MIDDLEWARE = (trace, authenticate) and reverse wrapping make it outermost.

nodes.label: Check demo access
nodes.detail: authenticate returns (403, {error: reader access required}, {}) when X-Demo-Access is not reader; otherwise it returns next_handler(request).

nodes.label: 403 rejection
nodes.detail: The rejection bypasses route, domain and store, then returns through trace.

nodes.label: Route and handler
nodes.detail: For the scoped GET /books, route returns (200, {books: reading_list(request[store])}, {}). Other paths are outside this scenario.

nodes.label: Published books
nodes.detail: reading_list filters stored rows by published flag.

nodes.label: Read SQLite rows
nodes.detail: ReadingStore.books selects titles and published flags ordered by title.

nodes.label: Handler result
nodes.detail: After reading_list returns, route constructs the 200 body; authenticate returns that result to trace.

nodes.label: Attach trace header
nodes.detail: After next_handler returns either 403 or 200, trace adds X-Request-Id and returns to do_GET.

nodes.label: JSON response
nodes.detail: do_GET serializes the admitted result or rejection to JSON with trace headers.

edges.label: dispatch
edges.detail: dispatch wraps registered middleware in reverse to preserve execution order.

edges.label: next
edges.detail: Trace invokes the next handler before annotating its response.

edges.label: missing access
edges.detail: Missing or incorrect public fixture sentinel returns 403 immediately.

edges.label: admitted
edges.detail: Accepted demo access invokes the route handler.

edges.label: reading_list
edges.detail: The books handler requests domain-filtered titles.

edges.label: books query
edges.detail: Domain obtains rows from the injected store.

edges.label: rows
edges.detail: The SQLite cursor provides published flags and titles.

edges.label: filtered titles
edges.detail: reading_list returns published titles to route, which forms the 200 body.

edges.label: return 200
edges.detail: The result unwinds through authenticate to the outer trace wrapper.

edges.label: return 403
edges.detail: The early authentication result returns directly to the outer trace wrapper.

edges.label: status + headers + body
edges.detail: dispatch returns the traced result; do_GET sends status/headers and writes json.dumps(body).

views.title: Declared local infrastructure
views.question: Where does declared local traffic enter and persist?
views.scope: Declared optional local Docker Compose environment; not a live deployment.
views.summary: HTTP crosses Nginx and the API; SQLite uses a file volume, not network traffic.

nodes.label: Host :8088
nodes.detail: Compose publishes host port 8088 to Nginx port 80.

nodes.label: API :8080
nodes.detail: The Python service runs server.py with READING_DB=/data/reading.sqlite.

nodes.label: SQLite volume
nodes.detail: The named reading-data volume stores the embedded SQLite database.

edges.label: HTTP api:8080
edges.detail: proxy_pass sends requests over the Compose network.

edges.label: SQLite file I/O
edges.detail: Embedded SQLite writes /data/reading.sqlite on the mounted volume.
